title: Delta Acceptor: Stability and Statistical Gate for FP8/INT8 Rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement an automated validation harness that applies robust, context-aware statistical gates for FP8/INT8 quantized rollouts. The harness will replay production-like cohorts against float (baseline) and quantized variants and compute a layered pass/fail decision using bootstrap confidence intervals, sequential testing (alpha-spending), and cohort-weighted utility scores. It must support: golden prompt cohorts, synthetic adversarial perturbations, per-cohort thresholding, regression attribution to layers/ops, and a compact JSON results contract consumed by the rollout controller. Deliverables: replay runner, metric engine, gate evaluator, CI integration for PRs, and runtime webhook to trigger canary failover.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay historical cohorts (text/chat/embedding) deterministically using stored seeds and produce comparable token-level traces between baseline and quantized models.

Metric engine computes at minimum: token-level logprobs delta, sequence-level perplexity delta, embedding cosine similarity distribution, KL diagnostics for distributional shifts, and a user-defined application metric (e.g., API-level F1 or rerank nDCG).

Gate evaluator implements: bootstrap 95% CI for mean deltas, sequential test with alpha-spend to allow staged canaries, and cohort-weighted utility scoring. Pass/Fail decisions exposed as boolean + rationale string in results JSON.
False-positive rate on synthetic no-regression cohorts < 2% across 1000 runs (stochastic environments controlled).
Integration tests in CI: a fake PR run against a small golden set that must fail if a large regression (>5% embedding cosine drop or >0.2 mean logprob delta) is introduced.
Console dashboard link (per-rollout) with distribution plots, top-k offending prompts, and recommended rollback action is available for manual review.
Rollout controller consumes results JSON and triggers automatic fallback to float baseline if gate fails during canary (configurable policy).
steps: Design result JSON contract and gate rule DSL (owner: Diego).
Implement deterministic replay runner that loads stored seeds, tokenizes consistently, and records per-token logprobs (owner: infra-ml).
Implement metric primitives: delta-logprob, perplexity, embedding-similarity distributions, top-k lexeme diff, and custom hooks for customers' app metrics (owner: evals).
Build statistical engine with bootstrap CI, sequential testing primitives, multiple-hypothesis correction, and cohort weighting logic (owner: stats).
Develop gate evaluator that composes metric results into pass/fail decisions and human-readable rationale using rules DSL (owner: platform).
Add CI job template and GitHub Actions workflow to run harness on PRs touching quant/compilation code (owner: sde).
Instrument telemetry and console panels: distribution histograms, swimlane of offending prompts, and per-layer attribution graphs (owner: observability).
Run internal fuzz + adversarial sweep and tune thresholds to meet acceptance criteria (owner: qa).
Soft-launch canary with 1% traffic, automated fallback enabled, monitor for two weeks and iterate (owner: release).
design_notes: We intentionally use bootstrap CIs rather than asymptotic z-tests because many metrics have heavy tails (embedding cosine similarity distributions are skewed).
Staged alpha-spend uses Pocock-style spending function so early canaries are conservative but global alpha budget is preserved for the rollout window.
Cohort weighting: prioritize recent production cohorts and those flagged as high-value (billing signals) using configurable weights in the gate DSL.
To reduce flakiness, replay runner caches tokenization mapping per model build and enforces deterministic RNG for sampling adversarial perturbations.
decisions: Use baseline float model as canonical reference for all comparisons (no ensemble of floats) — simplifies drift attribution.
Expose a gated DSL allowing product teams to set 'safety' vs 'utility' tradeoffs per rollout (e.g., embed-sim threshold vs mean logprob delta).
Adopt 95% bootstrap CI as primary statistical signal and use p-value fusion for secondary signals (embedding/perplexity).
Result JSON will include a small human-readable rationale plus machine-readable fields for automation; rationale includes top 10 offending prompts and suggested rollback cause tags.
tradeoffs: Strict statistical gates reduce rollout velocity for small improvements — we allow teams to lower sensitivity via DSL but default to conservative thresholds for P0 customers.
Running full replay against large cohorts is expensive; we will provide a fast-path small golden subset for PRs and a full cohort run for scheduled rollouts.
Bootstrapping increases runtime cost vs analytic approximations, but it reduces type-I errors under non-normal metric distributions.
